NASB.1: Now the Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded,
NASB.2: and he went out to meet Asa and said to him, 'Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: the LORD is with you when you are with Him. And if you seek Him, He will let you find Him; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
NASB.3: 'For many days Israel was without the true God and without a teaching priest and without law.
NASB.4: 'But in their distress they turned to the LORD God of Israel, and they sought Him, and He let them find Him.
NASB.5: 'In those times there was no peace to him who went out or to him who came in, for many disturbances afflicted all the inhabitants of the lands.
NASB.6: 'Nation was crushed by nation, and city by city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.
NASB.7: 'But you, be strong and do not lose courage, for there is reward for your work.'
NASB.8: Now when Asa heard these words and the prophecy which Azariah the son of Oded the prophet spoke, he took courage and removed the abominable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities which he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He then restored the altar of the LORD which was in front of the porch of the LORD.
NASB.9: He gathered all Judah and Benjamin and those from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who resided with them, for many defected to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
NASB.10: So they assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
NASB.11: They sacrificed to the LORD that day 700 oxen and 7,000 sheep from the spoil they had brought.
NASB.12: They entered into the covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and soul;
NASB.13: and whoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.
NASB.14: Moreover, they made an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets and with horns.
NASB.15: All Judah rejoiced concerning the oath, for they had sworn with their whole heart and had sought Him earnestly, and He let them find Him. So the LORD gave them rest on every side.
NASB.16: He also removed Maacah, the mother of King Asa, from the [position of] queen mother, because she had made a horrid image as an Asherah, and Asa cut down her horrid image, crushed [it] and burned [it] at the brook Kidron.
NASB.17: But the high places were not removed from Israel; nevertheless Asa's heart was blameless all his days.
NASB.18: He brought into the house of God the dedicated things of his father and his own dedicated things: silver and gold and utensils.
NASB.19: And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

NKJV.1: Now the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded.
NKJV.2: And he went out to meet Asa, and said to him: “Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you while you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
NKJV.3: For a long time Israel has been without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without law;
NKJV.4: but when in their trouble they turned to the LORD God of Israel, and sought Him, He was found by them.
NKJV.5: And in those times there was no peace to the one who went out, nor to the one who came in, but great turmoil was on all the inhabitants of the lands.
NKJV.6: So nation was destroyed by nation, and city by city, for God troubled them with every adversity.
NKJV.7: But you, be strong and do not let your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded!”
NKJV.8: And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and removed the abominable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities which he had taken in the mountains of Ephraim; and he restored the altar of the LORD that was before the vestibule of the LORD.
NKJV.9: Then he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those who dwelt with them from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, for they came over to him in great numbers from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
NKJV.10: So they gathered together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
NKJV.11: And they offered to the LORD at that time seven hundred bulls and seven thousand sheep from the spoil they had brought.
NKJV.12: Then they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
NKJV.13: and whoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel was to be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
NKJV.14: Then they took an oath before the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting and trumpets and rams’ horns.
NKJV.15: And all Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought Him with all their soul; and He was found by them, and the LORD gave them rest all around.
NKJV.16: Also he removed Maachah, the mother of Asa the king, from being queen mother, because she had made an obscene image of Asherah; and Asa cut down her obscene image, then crushed and burned it by the Brook Kidron.
NKJV.17: But the high places were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless the heart of Asa was loyal all his days.
NKJV.18: He also brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated and that he himself had dedicated: silver and gold and utensils.
NKJV.19: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

ESV.18: And he brought into the house of God the sacred gifts of his father and his own sacred gifts, silver, and gold, and vessels.
ESV.19: And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

CSB17.1: The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.2: So he went out to meet Asa and said to him, “Asa and all Judah and Benjamin, hear me. The LORD is with you <sup>ⓙ</sup> when you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, <sup>ⓚ</sup> but if you abandon him, he will abandon you. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.3: For many years Israel has been without the true God, <sup>ⓜ</sup> without a teaching priest, and without instruction, <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.4: but when they turned to the LORD God of Israel in their distress and sought him, he was found by them.
CSB17.5: In those times there was no peace for those who went about their daily activities because the residents of the lands had many conflicts.
CSB17.6: Nation was crushed by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every possible distress.
CSB17.7: But as for you, be strong; don’t give up, <sup>[1]</sup> for your work has a reward.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.8: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the abhorrent idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. <sup>ⓑ</sup> He renovated the altar of the LORD that was in front of the portico of the LORD’s temple. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.9: Then he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, as well as those from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who were residing among them, for they had defected to him from Israel in great numbers when they saw that the LORD his God was with him. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.10: They were gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
CSB17.11: At that time they sacrificed to the LORD seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep and goats from all the plunder they had brought. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.12: Then they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their ancestors with all their heart and all their soul. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.13: Whoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel would be put to death, young or old, <sup>[2]</sup> man or woman. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.14: They took an oath to the LORD in a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with rams’ horns.
CSB17.15: All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their mind. They had sought him with all their heart, and he was found by them. <sup>ⓗ</sup> So the LORD gave them rest on every side. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.16: King Asa <sup>ⓙ</sup> also removed Maacah, his grandmother, <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup> from being queen mother because she had made an obscene image of Asherah. Asa chopped down her obscene image, then crushed it and burned it in the Kidron Valley. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.17: The high places were not taken away from Israel; nevertheless, Asa was wholeheartedly devoted his entire life. <sup>[4]</sup>
CSB17.18: He brought his father’s consecrated gifts and his own consecrated gifts into God’s temple: silver, gold, and utensils.
CSB17.19: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.

WEB.1: The Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded:
WEB.2: and he went out to meet Asa, and said to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin! Yahweh is with you, while you are with him; and if you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
WEB.3: Now for a long time Israel was without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without law.
WEB.4: But when in their distress they turned to Yahweh, the God of Israel, and sought him, he was found by them.
WEB.5: In those times there was no peace to him who went out, nor to him who came in; but great troubles were on all the inhabitants of the lands.
WEB.6: They were broken in pieces, nation against nation, and city against city; for God troubled them with all adversity.
WEB.7: But you be strong, and don’t let your hands be slack; for your work will be rewarded.”
WEB.8: When Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominations out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed Yahweh’s altar that was before Yahweh’s porch.
WEB.9: He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those who lived with them out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon; for they came to him out of Israel in abundance when they saw that Yahweh his God was with him.
WEB.10: So they gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
WEB.11: They sacrificed to Yahweh in that day, of the plunder which they had brought, seven hundred head of cattle and seven thousand sheep.
WEB.12: They entered into the covenant to seek Yahweh, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul;
WEB.13: and that whoever would not seek Yahweh, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
WEB.14: They swore to Yahweh with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with cornets.
WEB.15: All Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found by them. Then Yahweh gave them rest all around.
WEB.16: Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king, he removed from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; so Asa cut down her image, ground it into dust, and burned it at the brook Kidron.
WEB.17: But the high places were not taken away out of Israel; nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
WEB.18: He brought the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, gold, and vessels into God’s house.
WEB.19: There was no more war to the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.

NLT.1: Then the Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded,
NLT.2: and he went out to meet King Asa as he was returning from the battle. “Listen to me, Asa!” he shouted. “Listen, all you people of Judah and Benjamin! The LORD will stay with you as long as you stay with him! Whenever you seek him, you will find him. But if you abandon him, he will abandon you.
NLT.3: For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach them, and without the Law to instruct them.
NLT.4: But whenever they were in trouble and turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought him out, they found him.
NLT.5: “During those dark times, it was not safe to travel. Problems troubled the people of every land.
NLT.6: Nation fought against nation, and city against city, for God was troubling them with every kind of problem.
NLT.7: But as for you, be strong and courageous, for your work will be rewarded.”
NLT.8: When Asa heard this message from Azariah the prophet, he took courage and removed all the detestable idols from the land of Judah and Benjamin and in the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. And he repaired the altar of the LORD, which stood in front of the entry room of the LORD’s Temple.
NLT.9: Then Asa called together all the people of Judah and Benjamin, along with the people of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had settled among them. For many from Israel had moved to Judah during Asa’s reign when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
NLT.10: The people gathered at Jerusalem in late spring, during the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
NLT.11: On that day they sacrificed to the LORD 700 cattle and 7,000 sheep and goats from the plunder they had taken in the battle.
NLT.12: Then they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and soul.
NLT.13: They agreed that anyone who refused to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death — whether young or old, man or woman.
NLT.14: They shouted out their oath of loyalty to the LORD with trumpets blaring and rams’ horns sounding.
NLT.15: All in Judah were happy about this covenant, for they had entered into it with all their heart. They earnestly sought after God, and they found him. And the LORD gave them rest from their enemies on every side.
NLT.16: King Asa even deposed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made an obscene Asherah pole. He cut down her obscene pole, broke it up, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
NLT.17: Although the pagan shrines were not removed from Israel, Asa’s heart remained completely faithful throughout his life.
NLT.18: He brought into the Temple of God the silver and gold and the various items that he and his father had dedicated.
NLT.19: So there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.

AMP.1: Now the Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded,
AMP.2: and he went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: the LORD is with you while you are with Him. If you seek Him [inquiring for and of Him, as your soul's first necessity], He will let you find Him; but if you abandon (turn away from) Him, He will abandon (turn away from) you.
AMP.3: Now for a long time Israel was without the true God and without a teaching priest, and without [God's] law.
AMP.4: But when they were in their trouble and distress they turned to the LORD God of Israel, and [in desperation earnestly] sought Him, and He let them find Him.
AMP.5: In those times there was no peace for him who went out or for him who came in, for great suffering came on all the inhabitants of the lands.
AMP.6: Nation was crushed by nation, and city by city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.
AMP.7: But as for you, be strong and do not lose courage, for there is reward for your work."
AMP.8: And when Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Azariah the son of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the repulsive idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities which he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. Then he restored the altar [of burnt offering] of the LORD which was in front of the porch [of the temple] of the LORD.
AMP.9: He gathered all Judah and Benjamin and the strangers who were with them out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, for they came over to Asa from Israel in large numbers when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
AMP.10: So they assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
AMP.11: They sacrificed to the LORD on that day from the spoil they had brought—700 oxen and 7,000 sheep.
AMP.12: They entered into a covenant (solemn agreement) to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and soul;
AMP.13: and that whoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.
AMP.14: They swore an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with [jubilant] shouting, with trumpets, and with horns.
AMP.15: All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and had sought Him with their whole heart, and He let them find Him. So the LORD gave them rest on every side.
AMP.16: He also removed Maacah, King Asa's mother, from the position of queen mother, because she had made a repulsive image for [the goddess] Asherah. Asa cut down her idol, crushed it, and burned it at the Brook Kidron.
AMP.17: But the high places [of pagan worship] were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless Asa's heart was blameless all his days.
AMP.18: He brought the things that his father [Abijah] had dedicated and those things that he had dedicated into the house of God—silver and gold and utensils.
AMP.19: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

NET.1: God’s Spirit came upon Azariah son of Oded.
NET.2: He met Asa and told him, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin! The LORD is with you when you are loyal to him. If you seek him, he will respond to you, but if you reject him, he will reject you.
NET.3: For a long time Israel had no true God, or priest to instruct them, or law.
NET.4: Because of their distress, they turned back to the LORD God of Israel. They sought him and he responded to them.
NET.5: In those days no one could travel safely, for total chaos had overtaken all the people of the surrounding lands.
NET.6: One nation was crushed by another, and one city by another, for God caused them to be in great turmoil.
NET.7: But as for you, be strong and don’t get discouraged, for your work will be rewarded.”
NET.8: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he was encouraged. He removed the detestable idols from the entire land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had seized in the Ephraimite hill country. He repaired the altar of the LORD in front of the porch of the LORD’s temple.
NET.9: He assembled all Judah and Benjamin, as well as the settlers from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had come to live with them. Many people from Israel had come there to live when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
NET.10: They assembled in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
NET.11: At that time they sacrificed to the LORD some of the plunder they had brought back, including 700 head of cattle and 7,000 sheep.
NET.12: They solemnly agreed to seek the LORD God of their ancestors with their whole heart and being.
NET.13: Anyone who would not seek the LORD God of Israel would be executed, whether they were young or old, male or female.
NET.14: They swore their allegiance to the LORD, shouting their approval loudly and sounding trumpets and horns.
NET.15: All Judah was happy about the oath, because they made the vow with their whole heart. They willingly sought the LORD and he responded to them. He made them secure on every side.
NET.16: King Asa also removed Maacah his grandmother from her position as queen mother because she had made a loathsome Asherah pole. Asa cut down her Asherah pole and crushed and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
NET.17: The high places were not eliminated from Israel, yet Asa was wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD throughout his lifetime.
NET.18: He brought the holy items that his father and he had made into God’s temple, including the silver, gold, and other articles.
NET.19: There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
